title: Count Them
lead: A sealed manifest has reached you from Commandant Halloran of Bastion Nine, with a note in his own tired handwriting. It says only: Count them.
anyone: Dockhands say a plain unmarked ship leaves the yards on the first of every month, full of people, with no way of telling anyone where it went. Commandant Halloran of Bastion Nine has started counting them, in his own tired handwriting.

gm.truth: Every month, plain unmarked hulls leave Bastion Nine and Vantor's Outer Yards, refuel at Mott Jessup's back dock, cross the border and cut their engines. Silver drones come gently out to meet them. The Regent has done this for twenty-two years and calls it a tax: a payment in people, for which the Choir leaves Vantor alone. On paper they're 'resettled to the Outer Colonies'. For years it was political prisoners. Now the prison yards are empty, the shipments have grown to nine hundred a month and rising, and that's the real reason for the Generous Offer: the refugees aren't soldiers. They're the coin. Clause 41(c) makes it legal, and captured Resonants go first, because they count for more. Dain Halloran has signed those transfers for years without ever asking where they go, and he knows he has never asked. He's done. Severa Lune stamped her own sister's contract without reading it, then saw her name on a transfer, and she has kept copies ever since. Corvane has seen it and wants out. Vael has never seen a manifest. She believes her prisoners go to Ministry custody, and the first time she reads one she'll recognize every full legal name. Jaska Moor has followed twelve tons of missing fuel to this door, and if someone shows her where those ships go she'll file a formal complaint, through channels, addressed to the Regency. It would get her killed, and it could shake the whole Hegemony. If the truth gets out, the hard question lands: everyone believes this is all that stands between the silver and a world of two billion people. Stop the ships and Vantor may be next. (out_vantor_unmarked is the handover seen up close.) Arc clues: unmarked_manifest, clause_41c, token_names.
beats: The manifest: names, ages, and a column headed Resettled. It has people on it the captain sent to Bastion themselves, or who left the fleet with the captain's blessing. The note's handwriting gets worse toward the end. Count them, and the numbers don't match anything anyone has ever been told.

Halloran in secret, sighing before he speaks: 'Officially, there are no such ships. That means I've signed for them every month for nine years.' Or Severa, who has been caught, or is about to be: 'Case four-four-one-nine was my sister. I didn't say that.' Moor is very polite about it.

Seeing it. Shadow an unmarked hull across the line. The engines cut, and there's a long quiet. Silver comes out without haste, the people aboard walk out in a line, and no one's shooting. It's the calmest thing the captain will ever see. Afterward, on the empty deck, there's a neat stack of silver discs, and they look just like the ones the Quiet hand out at Haven.
Vael. She can be shown the manifest, or she finds out. She reads every name aloud, in full. Then she takes off her gloves, and for once she doesn't apologize.

What now? Hit the next ship and free them? Publish it and bring down an empire with the silver right behind it? Use it as leverage? Thousands who signed are still on the Line, and Kit Marlowe-Dace has been buying contracts with borrowed money, one family at a time, for reasons they'd rather be shot than explain.
routes: Hacker: Bastion's shipping records and the real category tables (hacking), then the Ministry's own audit trail.
Pilot or gunner: shadow a hull across the line (piloting, stealth), or stop one (gunnery, tactics) and see who's aboard.

Infiltrator: go in as a refugee, sign the contract and get onto a list (deception, composure). It's the fastest way to see it, and the scariest way to find out whether your friends are paying attention.

Talker: give Corvane a way out in return for his testimony, get Halloran to put his name to it, buy Mott Jessup's copies with berths for his daughters (persuasion, commerce). Moor's one more question may be the one that helps.
Resonant: stand near a loaded hull and hear them (attunement). Vael, with her dampeners off, hears you hearing them. That's how the two of you meet for the second time.
checks: hacking:hard to reach Bastion's shipping records
piloting:hard to follow an unmarked hull across the line unseen
deception:hard to get onto a transfer list and stay alive
commerce:moderate to buy Mott's copies, or persuasion:hard to get Corvane's testimony
gunnery:moderate to disable a hull without killing anyone aboard
attunement:hard to hear what's in a loaded hull
fights: customs_marine and hegemony_hunter if the captain is caught at Bastion
ministry_blade if they get close to the manifests at the Outer Yards
outcomes: If a hull is stopped, hundreds are saved, there's a firefight with the Hegemony, and one payment is missed. Everyone watches the border for what happens next, and refugees flood back to a fleet that can't feed them.

If it's published through Garrick Fenn, the fleet and the Hegemony convulse and signing stops. Bastion riots. Halloran is arrested or escapes. The Regent is unmoved, and now moves against the fleet openly.

If Vael turns, she walks out of the Ministry and she's the most dangerous ally anyone could have. She won't take off her dampeners, not yet. If she doesn't turn, she goes to the Regent to ask, and comes back believing it's necessary, which is far worse.

If Moor is shown it, she files her complaint, in triplicate. What happens next depends on who is protecting her. It's the first legal challenge to the Regency in a thousand years, and it's about twelve tons of fuel.
If it's kept quiet as leverage, the captain can use it on Corvane or the Regent, and they've just become part of the system. Severa's fate is on them.
gm.rewards: The manifests, forged_papers from Severa, a signal_scrambler from Mott, the fleet's trust, and the end of any standing with the hegemony.
